blocks.content: Now, let's learn about our final selector: the ID selector.
Sometimes, you may want to style only a specific, unique part of a webpage, such as a header or footer. To achieve this, you can use the ID selector.
The ID selector targets a single HTML element with a unique identifier (ID) and applies specific styles to it.
In CSS, the ID selector is specified using the hash (#) character, followed by the id of the HTML element.

In this example, the ID selector #main-header applies styles only to the unique <header> element with the id="main-header".
Similarly, the #main-footer selector targets the unique <footer> element with the id="main-footer".
Even though you might have multiple sections or paragraphs in the document, only the unique header and footer are affected by these ID-specific styles.
